title: Maximum Average Subarray I
prompt: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. Find the contiguous subarray of length `k` that has the maximum average value, and return that maximum average. Any answer within `10^-5` of the actual answer is accepted.

examples.explanation: The subarray [12,-5,-6,50] has the maximum average (12-5-6+50)/4 = 12.75.
All values are negative, so the best window is the one that minimizes the loss: [-1,-2], averaging -1.5

hints: Recomputing the sum of every length-k window from scratch is O(n*k) — most of that work is redundant.
Use a fixed-size sliding window: keep a running sum of the current k elements.
When the window slides by one, update the sum in O(1) by subtracting the element that leaves and adding the element that enters, instead of resumming.

solution.approach: Compute the sum of the first k elements as the initial window. Then slide the window one element at a time across the array: each step adds the new right element and subtracts the element leaving on the left, keeping the running sum updated in O(1). Track the maximum sum seen and divide by k at the end.
solution.code:
def find_max_average(nums, k):
    window_sum = sum(nums[:k])
    max_sum = window_sum
    for i in range(k, len(nums)):
        window_sum += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
        max_sum = max(max_sum, window_sum)
    return max_sum / k
